head: f1c8120b3c3d2be7c49788c6532366bccc166c56
title: Round the basket total once, in pennies
reason: A new test pins the three-line total that was a penny out, and the basket view still needs a person to look at it.

lead.text: A basket of three lines at a third of a pound showed 0.99 instead of 1.00, because each line and then the sum rounded. The total now adds whole pennies and divides once, in `src/cart.ts`.

signals.summary: The basket total reads the rounded amount once
The unit suite passed on this head
A new test proves the three-line total; nothing tests a price below a penny
Reverting restores the double rounding; it writes no data
Root cause named; the author reports the test failing before the fix

rows.label: symptom
rows.text: Three lines at 0.33, 0.33 and 0.34 showed a total of 0.99.

rows.label: root-cause
rows.text: `lineTotal` rounded each line to pennies and `total` rounded the sum again, so the errors added up.

rows.label: reproduction
rows.text: The new test in `src/cart.test.ts` builds the three-line basket.

rows.label: before
rows.text: Reported by the author: the test failed on the base commit.

rows.label: after
rows.text: The unit suite passed on this head.

rows.label: not-checked
rows.text: Prices with fractions of a penny, which `src/cart.ts:5` rounds per unit.

rows.label: left-open
rows.text: Saved baskets keep the total they were stored with until they are repriced.

testing.summary: The new test proves the basket total no longer rounds twice. It does not prove what happens to a price below a penny.
proves: The total adds whole pennies before dividing
gaps: A price with a fraction of a penny
also: The unit suite passed on this head

risks.title: A price with a fraction of a penny rounds per unit
risks.impact: Ten items at 0.125 now total 1.30 rather than 1.25, because each unit rounds before the quantity multiplies.

decisions.question: Should a price with fractions of a penny round per unit?
decisions.why: It decides what a bulk order of cheap items costs.
decisions.suggestion: Round the line, not the unit: multiply first, then round once per line.

areas.name: UI
areas.summary: The basket view reads the total once and formats it.

after.text: Reprice saved baskets once the fix is live

guardrails.title: Money still moves as floating-point numbers
guardrails.body: `total` divides pennies back into a float, so the next change that adds a discount can round twice again.
guardrails.proposal: A lint rule that fails a new `Math.round` on a money value outside `src/cart.ts`.
guardrails.evidence: Two rounding fixes touched `src/cart.ts` this month.

guardrails.title: No test runs prices below a penny
guardrails.body: The suite only builds whole-penny prices, so R1 had nothing to catch it.
guardrails.proposal: A table test over fractional prices and quantities that fails on per-unit rounding.

refactoring.title: Store prices as whole pennies
refactoring.body: Every caller converts floats to pennies and back. Storing pennies removes the conversion.
refactoring.proposal: Make `Line.price` an integer number of pennies and format only in the view.

noise.title: The UI was flagged for a one-line refactor
noise.body: `src/ui/Total.tsx` only names the amount before formatting it, yet the page wants a person to look at it.
noise.proposal: Treat a view change with no markup change as needing no recording.
